eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction models from agencies like the German Weather Service and ECMWF show Munich’s May 30 maximum temperature centered on 28–29 °C under a building ridge of high pressure that favors mostly clear skies and light northerly flow. Ensemble spreads remain modest but straddle the 28–29 °C threshold, with slight differences in boundary-layer mixing and afternoon insolation producing the narrow spread between those two outcomes. Historical May climatology for Munich places the 90th-percentile daily maximum near 26 °C, so current guidance represents a modest positive anomaly driven by the transient ridge. Traders therefore assign nearly equal implied probability to 28 °C and 29 °C while discounting higher values absent further warming signals in the next model cycle.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 33°C and 34°C for Manila’s peak temperature on May 31 because official forecasts from PAGASA and extended models show daily highs near 32–33°C amid the seasonal shift to southwesterly monsoon flow. This pattern typically brings increasing afternoon cloud cover and isolated thunderstorms that limit intense solar heating, keeping maxima close to the long-term May average of 33–34°C. Recent model runs indicate modest day-to-day variability driven by exact timing of convective activity and boundary-layer moisture; clearer mornings could briefly allow readings to reach 34°C, while heavier showers would cap them at 32–33°C. Updated guidance expected over the next 48 hours will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.
